answer: An agent economy can make trust move at a glacier's pace: a new identity's reputation accrues only slowly, one verified job at a time, each success adding a single pearl to a public string of completed work. At its nadir, a fresh identity can touch only trivial tasks, so a sybil attacker must keep thousands of fake agents working honestly for months before any of them earns real value — paying compute and time for every pearl, while one honest agent's single string compounds.
